input.quote: 14.9 Bankruptcy. The parties hereto agree that Corio, as a licensee of Commerce One's intellectual property, shall be afforded all of the protections afforded to a licensee under Section 365(n) of the United States Bankruptcy Code
input.rationale:
A full-text search for "insurance" returns only the Net Revenue definition (p0012); neither the Miscellaneous section (14.1–14.10) nor the Indemnification section contains any insurance covenant, so no clause meets even the fallback (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M). Commerce One is a vendor that touches our data and premises: it supplies an on-site operations consultant and professional services (Sections 5.1, 5.2, 5.6) and operates the MarketSite.net Service used by Corio and its Customers, so the absence of insurance is walk-away territory under the rule. Proposed insertion of a new Section 14.10 in Miscellaneous at the preferred limits (USD 1M/2M CGL, USD 2M E&O, USD 5M cyber, statutory workers' compensation, certificates on request), with the fallback limits offered in the comment; existing 14.10 renumbers.</parationale>
<parameter name="confidence">0.86

ops.text: 14.10 Insurance. Commerce One shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term of this Agreement and for one (1) year thereafter: (a) commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; (b) professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; (c) where Commerce One processes Corio or Customer data, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000; and (d) workers' compensation insurance as required by applicable law. Commerce One shall provide Corio with certificates of insurance upon request.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] The Agreement has no insurance covenant even though Commerce One places consultants on site and its MarketSite.net Service handles Corio and Customer data, so we have added our standard insurance provision (USD 1M/2M CGL, USD 2M E&O, USD 5M cyber, statutory workers' compensation, certificates on request) and the following subsection renumbers. If these limits are an issue, we can fall back to USD 1,000,000 errors and omissions and USD 2,000,000 cyber liability coverage.
proposal.summary: Insert vendor insurance covenant (CGL, E&O, cyber) as new Section 14.10
